name: libprotoident
desc: Performs application layer protocol identification for flows
why: Identifies application protocols from flow data, a fascinating door into how traffic reveals its own identity.

brief.what_it_is: Libprotoident is a C library that labels each network flow with the application protocol it most likely carries, such as BitTorrent, SMTP, or POP3. It works from the first four bytes of application payload sent in each direction, not from full packet contents. It ships three command-line tools (lpi_protoident, lpi_find_unknown, and lpi_arff) that read a libtrace URI, which can be a trace file or a live network interface. lpi_protoident prints one line per flow to stdout, with the protocol label, endpoints, ports, transport protocol, timestamps, byte counts, and the first four payload bytes per direction.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a library for application protocol identification, built so that programmers can write their own tools that use protocol information. It also notes that some traffic patterns in the WAND group's trace sets cannot be tied to any known protocol, and asks readers for help naming them.
brief.how_it_works: The library matches patterns in the first four bytes of application payload sent from each endpoint. The tools use libflowmanager to track flows, and identification happens only when a flow concludes or expires. Flows can also be grouped into categories, so BitTorrent, Gnutella, and eMule all fall under P2P, and SMTP, POP3, and IMAP fall under Mail.

brief.install_notes: Requires libtrace 4.0.1 or later, available from github.com/LibtraceTeam/libtrace. libflowmanager 3.0.0 or later is optional for the library but required to build the tools; it is available from github.com/LibtraceTeam/libflowmanager. Standard autotools build: configure, make, make install. No accounts or runtime services are mentioned. The README does not describe first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It identifies protocols from only the first four payload bytes in each direction, a deliberately minimal form of deep packet inspection that works on flow records without decrypting or reassembling streams. It also ships an ARFF exporter so flow features can feed machine learning directly.
brief.status: Unknown from the README alone. It shows version 2.0.15 and copyright dates from 2011 to 2020, but gives no release date and no last-commit date. Bug reports point to a separate github.com/wanduow/libprotoident repository.
brief.caveats: Only the first four payload bytes per direction are examined, so the method is inherently limited. Identification happens only after a flow ends or expires, so it is poor for real-time use. Some traffic is labelled only as unidentified 'mystery' patterns. The tools need libflowmanager, which adds a dependency. The README names COPYING and COPYING.LESSER for licensing but does not state the license in its text. The full list of supported protocols is kept on a wiki page that was not fetched.
quotes: using a very limited form of deep packet inspection, i.e. using the first four bytes of application payload sent in each direction
Identification only occurs when the flow has concluded or expired, so it is not very effective for real-time applications.
The library provides a simple API that will enable programmers to develop their own tools that utilise application protocol information
